key_insight: Distilling a fixed atomistic foundation model into compact potentials preserves key semiconductor-interface responses while improving simulation speed and accessible system size by orders of magnitude.
engineering_relevance: Compact distilled potentials enable large-scale studies of interfacial heat transport and mechanical failure with responses close to DFT-trained counterparts.
method: Select an EquiformerV3 teacher from 128 pretrained models across 22 families.
Train ACE and NEP students without target-specific teacher fine-tuning.
Compare against DFT-trained students using matched training configurations and architectures.
evidence_signal: Tests on 79,920-atom BAs/GaN interfaces and 29,792-atom Cu/diamond specimens showed deviations from DFT-trained counterparts of at most 6.6% in thermal conductance, 2.8% in tensile strength, and 1.5% in loading work.
watch_item: Committee-based selection improved high-error force fitting but did not consistently improve downstream properties, underscoring the need for application-level validation.
paper_title: Distilling an atomistic foundation model is all you need for large-scale molecular dynamics of semiconductor interfaces
